call.content:
Partner shortlist — Acme Orders
3 shortlisted from 5 looked at, for integration

## Shortlist
- Ledgerly — https://ledgerly.example/integrations — small-business bookkeeping — small shops — integration — a public API and a marketplace listing form on the integrations page.
- ShipQuick — https://shipquick.example/partners — shipping labels for small shops — the same shops — integration, co-marketing — a partner page with an apply form and joint webinars listed.
- Countly POS — https://countly.example/about — a point-of-sale app for market stalls — the same buyers at a smaller size — integration — public API docs; no programme named.

## Why each
- Ledgerly: both sell to small shops; an order in Acme becomes an invoice in Ledgerly, which their page already does for two order tools; the marketplace form is the way in.
- ShipQuick: a shop that takes orders in Acme prints labels in ShipQuick; their page lists three order tools and a webinar with one; the apply form is the way in.
- Countly: a stall that sells in person through Countly and online through Acme wants one stock count; the API docs are public; nobody is named.

## First contact
- Ledgerly (Sam Oduya, Partnerships, named on the page): "Your integrations page lists Orderline and Shoply for order-to-invoice, which is what our customers ask us for most. Acme Orders runs ordering for about the same shops, and an order becoming a Ledgerly invoice would save them the re-typing. Is the marketplace form the right way to start, or is there someone to talk to first?"
- ShipQuick (the partnerships team): "Your September webinar with Orderline on same-day labels is the workflow our shops use, with Acme in Orderline's place. Acme Orders is ordering for small shops; a label from an Acme order is the obvious join. Would an integration be a fit for the partner programme?"
- Countly (the partnerships team): "Your API docs show stock levels as a first-class object, which is the thing our online shops want to share with a stall. Acme Orders handles their online orders. Is there someone who looks after integrations with order tools?"

## Checked
- 3 searches; 4 fetches; 1 link not opened (https://stockwise.example/partners answered 404); excluded: Shopwise (competitor), Orderline (competitor).

script.say:
3 shortlisted from 5 looked at, for integration.

## Report
- 3 searches, 4 fetches; wrote "Partner shortlist — Acme Orders"
